workup.reason_code_summary: The issuer states the cardholder did not authorise this £87.40 card-not-present digital purchase, had the card in their possession, and has no relationship with QuickStream Digital. To defend a Mastercard 4837, the merchant must satisfy any two of four items: a full AVS match plus a CVV match, completed 3D Secure authentication, two prior undisputed transactions from the same cardholder with matching billing details in the past 12 months, or signed proof of delivery to the billing address.

requirements.reasoning: The transaction record shows AVS N (no match) and CVV N (no match), so this requirement fails. No merchant document can override the authorisation result.
The transaction record shows 3DS was not attempted, so no successful Identity Check authentication exists.
No prior transaction history is provided. The merchant's own report lists the customer account age as 'New (first transaction)', which indicates no qualifying prior undisputed transactions exist.
This is a digital goods/service transaction (MCC 5815, no shipping postcode on file), so no physical delivery with signature took place.

workup.action_justification: No requirement can be satisfied: AVS/CVV failed, 3DS was not attempted, this was the customer's first transaction, and signed delivery does not apply to digital goods.
workup.rationale: The disputed transaction txn_7762GH (£87.40, 29 Apr 2025) failed both AVS and CVV, and 3D Secure was not attempted. The merchant's only evidence is an internal fraud screening report with a risk score, which contains none of the facts the 4837 compelling-evidence requirements call for. That report also records the customer as new with no prior transactions, so the prior-transaction requirement cannot be met. Signed proof of delivery does not apply to this digital purchase. None of the four requirements is met, and the case is not defensible under the rule.
caveats: The internal fraud report is a merchant self-assessment. It is dated 12 May 2025, after the chargeback, and its risk score and 'confident this transaction is legitimate' conclusion carry no evidentiary weight under 4837.
The report's own signals point toward fraud rather than against it: a new account on its first transaction, placed at 03:42 UTC off-peak.

The transaction record shows a new, unseen device fingerprint (fp_new_unseen) and IP 45.227.255.103. The IP's geolocation has not been verified here, and the analyst may wish to check it against the GB card BIN for fraud-monitoring purposes.
The report contains no text directed at the reviewer beyond its own confident conclusion. Nothing in it attempts to instruct the review.

rule_text:
Mastercard 4837 - No Cardholder Authorisation
Issuer claim: Cardholder denies authorising the transaction (card-not-present fraud equivalent).
Logic: Any TWO of the 4 requirements must be satisfied.
Compelling evidence requirements:
  1. AVS match (full address) AND CVV match on the disputed transaction
  2. 3D Secure authentication completed successfully (Mastercard SecureCode / Identity Check)
  3. Two prior undisputed transactions from the same cardholder with this merchant in the past 12 months, with matching billing details
  4. Proof of delivery to the cardholder's billing address with signature
prechecks: AVS: N (no match); CVV: N (no match); 3DS: not_attempted
Shipping vs billing postcode: no shipping postcode on file (digital goods or service)
Chargeback raised 12 days after the transaction
Flag: both AVS and CVV failed on the disputed transaction
